To: Senator Joseph Baldacci, Representative Suzanne Salisbury, and Honorable members of the committee From: Audrey Piltch Re: Testimony in Support of LD 135, An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State

Esteemed members of the committee, I write to you as a girl raised in Maine who now is continuing my education at university in a city where I am very conscious of my experience as a woman.

Throughout high school and even largely into middle school, I was always aware of

moving through the world as a girl--it shows up in little moments that you can't put your finger

on, the overt and disheartening headlines, and even well into my classes at college, where

women can be reduced to numbers and statistics in horrific historical events. As a 19-year-old, I

want to feel safe and seen in my home state.

We've made incredible progress but still more work needs to be put forth, especially in a

new age of repealed protections and pushback to the equality movement. This extends to the

small actions, like the fair compensation for the dedicated members of the Permanent

Commission on the Status of Women.

Let us show up for Maine's citizens, especially those who are lacking opportunities and

equality, including all of our women of color, immigrant women, queer women, mothers, and

women facing discrimination. Change comes in small steps, and equal pay is essential to

supporting those who can champion that change.

Again, I hope to feel my voice heard in Maine, and therefore urge you to vote "ought to pass" on LD 135.

Respectfully submitted, Audrey Piltch Freeport

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT L.D. 135 "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State"
February 10, 2025 Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, Members of the State and Local Government Committee, my name is Darylen Cote. I have been a Commissioner on Maine's Permanent Commission on the Status of Women for five years. I was appointed to seat #12 pre-COVID and was subsequently reappointed. I am writing to support L.D. 135, "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State."
Of the 19 Commission members, I am one of only four who live north of Bangor. As a proud resident of Caribou in Aroostook County, I particularly represent the needs of rural women and the ability to have a voice on a Commission such as this. It has been my experience that the cost of participation is a barrier to me and many of my friends, neighbors and colleagues. There is no reimbursement available for actual dollars spent out of pocket for necessities such as accommodations, meals or travel expenses when inperson events are called for. The last time I needed to attend in person the only hotel room I could find was a little over $200, and you all know the price of gasoline and meals in a restaurant. From Caribou to Augusta and return is approximately 480 miles. I gladly volunteer my time to do this work for the women of Maine, especially the women in my rural, isolated part of Maine. However, being retired and on a fixed income, the added actual cost is a burden and barrier to maximum involvement in the work - as it would be for most people in the northern and other parts of Maine that are sparsely populated, and that struggle with poverty.
I support this bill because it would help to even the possibilities for adequate representation from all parts of Maine on the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women. We all deserve to have our voices heard equitably. The lack of reimbursement for actual expenses, and even for some portion of time, should not remain a barrier to that goal.
Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.
Sincerely, Darylen Cote

February 10, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government,
I join you today on behalf of the Maine Women's Lobby. Since 1978, the Maine Women's Lobby has worked to build gender justice in Maine through legislative advocacy and systems change. We are before you today In Support of LD 135 An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State. Thank you to President Daughty for sponsoring this important bill.
Many of our government structures weren't originally built with women in mind. The imprint of those early decisions still exists today, even when so much has been done to move us forward. Despite progress, gender is still a key driver in the health, wellness, and economic security of Mainers.
 In 2023, Governor Mills and the Dept. of Labor pointed out that the median income for full time, working women in Maine is still nearly $10,000 than the average income for men1 - the gap is far higher for women of color2, and it has widened since 20163.
 In 2022, only 65.6% of pregnant Black Mainers and 87% of pregnant white Mainers received "adequate prenatal care"4 - while the US has the highest maternal mortality rate in the developed world5. The systemic nature of these realities are clear: Since 2015, Maine has seen the closure of seven obstetrics units6, with an eighth closing in 20257 and a ninth suspending birthing services8 starting March 1, 2025.

 Nearly one-quarter of Mainers have experienced rape or attempted rape in their lifetime, women at more than three times the rate of men (35.7% vs 10.1%).9
These are all systemic challenges, and they need and deserve systemic solutions, embedded in state government.
Maine's Permanent Commission on the Status of Women is a key body helping to create systemic change. A body devoted to gendered data collection and report creation has an exponential impact on other governmental agencies as well as programmatic and policy-focused organizations: the work done by the Commission is important in its own right, and it informs the work done by so many groups across the state. Further, especially poignant in a moment when research and reports from Federal agencies devoted to inclusion and anti-discrimination are being wiped by the new Presidential Administration10, having a consistent home for gendered data collection is fundamental to ensuring Maine is making consistent progress on gender equity.
We are thrilled that the Commission now has one full time employee, for the first time since the 1990s. We have already seen the benefits of a devoted and focused leader and facilitator for the otherwise fully volunteer Commission. And despite the limitations of being a fully volunteer group, the Commission has done significant and essential work. However, the limitations of fully volunteer, unpaid Commissioners are clear on both sides of the coin. First, the ability to volunteer one's time unpaid is too often a barrier to participation in activities. Compensation for public service is central to ensuring equitable and accessibility representation and civic engagement. Additionally, providing compensation for Commissioner's efforts recognizes the value they provide to the State of Maine.
It's time for the state to invest meaningful resources to ensure that government structures and branches have gender equity as part of a systemic focus, that they are adequately staffed and funded, and that data be collected, analyzed, and presented in accessible ways across departments. Providing compensation for members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women is critical to continuing to create the systemic investments needed to create the necessary systemic change we need in Maine.
We hope you will vote Ought to Pass on LD 135. Thank you for your consideration.
 Sincerely,
Lily Bohen James, Advocacy Coordinator

THE MAINE SENATE 132nd Legislature

3 State House Station Augusta, Maine 04333

February 10, 2025
Testimony of Senate President Mattie Daughtry introducing
LD 135, "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State"
Presented to the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government, my name is Mattie Daughtry. I serve as President of the Maine Senate and proudly represent Senate District 23 in the Legislature, which includes Brunswick, Freeport, Harpswell, Pownal, Chebeague Island, and part of Yarmouth. I am here to introduce LD 135, "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State."
This bill changes the language that states Commission members cannot receive compensation for serving. It allows members of the Commission to receive compensation equal to the legislative per diem and be reimbursed for qualified expenses.
Maine's Permanent Commission on the Status of Women provides a critical service for the people of Maine. It is charged with generating a bi-annual report and shining a spotlight on how Maine's women are faring in our modern economy and more. The non-partisan, independent Commission also advocates for policies that improve opportunities for women and girls, and offers guidance on how we can better support them. Since its creation in the 125th Legislature, however, the work done by the Commissioners is done while balancing all of life's many other demands.
This bill seeks to provide members with the same per diem that we get in the Legislature and would ensure that commission-related expenses won't come out of these volunteers' pockets. It is ironic that the organization whose research tells us that unpaid caregiving work largely falls on Maine women and that full-time women workers make 83% of what men make, is doing its work largely unpaid with barely the resources to reimburse its contributors for a sandwich. Members of the Commission serve from every corner of this state. There is wonderful regional representation. Current members make the commitment and drive from Caribou, Pittston, Harrison, Dover-Foxcroft among other towns--it is important we encourage and support rural representation.
In their December report on women's labor and economic security, the commission found that despite progress, Maine women still earn less and are more likely to live in poverty.

The scope of the Commission is more important than ever but is compromised by a lack of funding. The message we send by not supporting its work is damaging. Anyone listening to this testimony who has a daughter would be forgiven for being deeply concerned about the future. This bill is a good start to allaying those fears. Maine needs the unvarnished, data-driven information provided by the Commission. My hope is that one day we can provide staffing in order to broaden the scope and increase the output of the Commission. In the meantime, providing Commission volunteers with this reasonable token of appreciation and respect will make it easier for them to continue their vital work. Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to take questions.

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT
L.D. 135 "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the State"

Testimony of Shenna Bellows Secretary of State
Department of the Secretary of State
February 10, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, Members of the State and Local Government Committee, my name is Shenna Bellows, I reside in Manchester, and I am the Secretary of State. I am here with Elinor
Higgins, the Executive Director of Maine's Permanent Commission on the Status of Women. We are speaking in support of L.D. 135 "An Act to Provide Compensation to Members of the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Enhance Equitable Commission Participation from Across the
State."
Currently, the 19 appointed members of the Commission are not authorized to receive per diem payments
or reimbursement for travel expenses incurred while serving the Women of Maine. While we recognize
that this does not present a challenge for every Commission member, it is a barrier to the robust participation of some members -- or potential members -- whose voices and experiences are critical for
meeting the Commission's purpose of improving opportunities for women across Maine. While the
Commission holds most of its meetings in a virtual setting, it convenes in person once each year for a planning meeting and members are encouraged to attend events in Augusta or elsewhere throughout the state to learn about the issues facing women, to meet with legislators, or to promote the work of the Commission. Currently, Commission members reside across 9 of Maine's counties, from York to Aroostook. The burden of unreimbursed travel falls disproportionately on the Commission members who reside far from Maine's urban centers - and who represent Maine's rural women. In some cases, rural Commission members have also had to pay out of pocket for overnight lodging in order to attend
Commission events. We know this is an issue that state legislators - especially those from Maine's rural
areas -- know well.
This bill would make it possible for us to support Commission members from across the state to ensure fairer participation in the Commission's work -- and fair representation for the voices of rural women. It would also authorize a per diem for Commission member participation in bi-monthly virtual meetings throughout the year. Commission members work in various sectors of the Maine economy, and for some, taking time off from work to attend a Commission meeting means losing needed income.
We appreciate your consideration of this important bill -- it will support positive outcomes for Maine
women, especially working women, low-income women, and rural women. I am happy to take any questions and we will be available for the work session if needed.
